  Parks, Recreation and Community Services

DATE:  July 22, 2020

TO:  Arts Commission

FROM:  Parks, Recreation and Community Services Department

SUBJECT:  Fairview Heights Public Art Plan: Rise Above
________________________________________________________________

RECOMMENDATION
It is recommended the Arts Commission recommend the City Council and Planning
Commission approve the Public Art Plan by art consultants NOWArt LA. for the Fairview
Heights mixed-use development at 923 E. Redondo Boulevard.

BACKGROUND
The Fairview Heights Public Art Plan is submitted to comply with the Percent for Arts
ordinance. The Arts Commission’s role is to review and comment on the developer’s plan
and make a recommendation to the Planning Commission and City Council regarding the
proposed art. Upon approval by the Planning Commission, the matter will be considered by
the City Council.

Fairview Heights is a mixed-use development at 923 E. Redondo Boulevard designed for
residential and commercial activity. The project provides quality affordable housing for
working families and special needs populations. Developers LINC Housing, National
CORE, Los Angeles County, LA Metro, and the City have collaborated on realizing the 100-
unit facility.

The developer team contracted art consultants NOWArt LA to propose a public art plan for
the facility. The consultants presented their preliminary proposal to the Arts Commission in
November 2019, identifying the public art area on the property’s eastern edge overlooking
a street-level plaza. The art plan spans on two architectural planes, punctuated by windows
of residential units. The City Planning Department calculated the percent for art valuation
as $153,000, based solely on the commercial building costs.

DISCUSSION
Rise Above is a three-part artwork by Ryan (Yanoe) Sarfati and Eric (Zoueh) Skotnes
developed to meet the City’s percent for art requirement. The artwork is a painted mural,
LED-lit clear panels that are attached to the walls and circling the mural in a nightly light
show, and an Augmented Reality (AR) application for iPhone and Android systems.

  Mural: The four-story mural is over 47 feet tall and 50 feet wide on two adjoining
  walls. The art wraps two sides of the residential tower and continues for 12’ onto
  an adjacent, slightly shorter, windowless wall above a plaza. Six windows
  punctuate the tower art area. The mural is a visual collage of diverse intertwined

  1
   forearms and hands, California poppy flowers and dramatic clouds on a field of
  green leaves and abstracted blue shapes. The mural will be painted with Benjamin
  Moore exterior acrylic paints with a 50-year warranty.

  LED-lit Panels: Eighteen translucent, etched panels frame the work with a
  dimensional, curving gesture around the two walls. These overlapped panels form
  a gesture derived from a Fibonacci sequence. Each panel is seated in exterior
  grade electric channel holding light-emitting diode (LED) strips. Each panel is
  etched with a traditional Aztec and African symbol. This etching diffuses the
  programmable LED pinpoint lights to create a lacy, mantilla-like effect on the
  layers. Panels range from 2’ to 10’ on the longest side with interior curved edges.

  Augmented Reality: An Augmented Reality (AR) application, downloaded onto a
  mobile device, is intended to enhance the onsite art experience. An exploratory
  community engagement phase compiled content and community response to the
  purpose of the art and residential facility. Sample questions were: What does home
  mean to you? What is important about having a home? What do you love about
  living in Inglewood? The artists propose the AR will include animations, video and
  voiceover of Inglewood community youth and elders.

  Note AR is a temporal format. It requires a smart phone with a current operating
  system and a supporting website or media host. In the Plan, the AR is separated
  from the project budget to reflect this temporal nature. Plans for AR content and
  publicity is to be determined so it is cited as a Public Art option at this time.

Proposal Assessment
The Art Commission’s role is to assess the proposal for five key public art components:
narrative content, design, location, artists’ expertise and budget.
Narrative Content: The proposed artwork’s relationship to the site architecture and
community is to be clear and compelling.
Rise Above provides a compelling compliment to the facility, community, and City. It fulfills
the requirement by addressing LINC Housing’s goals to provide a strong foundation for
educational attainment and economic mobility for lower income and special needs
residents.

Artwork Design: The public art is designed for the site, made of permanent maintainable
materials and sited to facilitate maintenance access.

The artwork site is two exterior walls facing the new Metro Downtown Inglewood Station
and the rail line. It will be highly visible from rail and auto commuter traffic on Redondo and
Florence Boulevards. It receives significant daytime sunlight and has a well-designed
lighting plan for night.

  2
   The mural uses permanent outdoor paints on exterior walls with residential and commercial
  windows. The acrylic panels and LEDs bring commercial signage and innovation, to the
  proposal. The time-based AR aspect builds on current Android and Apple technology, and
  is planned to incorporate community voices and stories, especially Inglewood youth.

  Site: The art site must be visually accessible to the general public.
  The artwork’s physical location, on east and south facing walls above an open plaza, is
  highly visible to vehicular and transit traffic travelling west along Redondo and Florence
  Boulevards and the Metro rail line. The art is above areas designed to welcome facility
  residents home and inspire the City’s other residents and visitors with this art experience.

  Also, the art site faces the Metro transit station where travelers will access downtown
  Inglewood, City Hall, the LA Phil YOLA building, and connect to the planned stadium district
  people movers for games and the opening and closing ceremonies for the 2028 Olympiad.
  The site is well chosen.

  Artist(s): The proposed public art is made by experienced, professional artist(s), as
  evidenced from past public art commissions and exhibitions.
  Ryan (Yanoe) Sarfati and Eric (Zoueh) Skotnes are college-trained in fine art, graphic
  design and illustration. Each transitioned to professional practice prior to formal graduation.
  They have completed exterior visual art projects for commercial and non-profit clients and
  pieces for entertainment industry clients, and Augmented Reality (AR) commissions. Their
  individual and combined experience exceeds the requirement.

  Budget: The Art Plan budget must meet or exceed the percent for art valuation, with
  preponderance of expenses to artists and their materials.
  The percent for art requirement is $153,000. The developer budgeted $200,000 for this
  effort. The Art budget exceeds the percent for art requirement even if the AR is unrealized
  and/or contingency allocation is unspent.

  DESCRIPTION OF ATTACHMENT:
  1. Fairview Heights Public Art Plan submitted by NOWArt LA

Sabrina Barnes, Parks, Recreation & Community Services Director
Helen Lessick, Public Art Consultant
Carmen Zella, Now Art LA

   CITY OF INGLEWOOD
  Parks, Recreation and Community Services

DATE:  July 22, 2020

TO:  Arts Commission

FROM:  Parks, Recreation and Community Services Department

SUBJECT: IGAP 2020: Inglewood Love
______________________________________________________________________

RECOMMENDATION
It is recommended the Arts Commission support the allocation of $12,000 for the
Inglewood Growing Artists Projects (IGAP) 2020 program to provide for purchases of
original artworks on paper by Inglewood artists as the Inglewood Love collection, to be
framed and displayed in public areas in City facilities.

BACKGROUND
Inglewood’s Cultural Masterplan Plan, and the subsequent Public Art Fund, direct the City
to develop opportunities for artists. Inglewood Growing Artists Projects (IGAP) is the
City’s public art effort to address that goal. IGAP has contributed permanent public art,
books and temporary and performed projects to the City since it began in 2014.

Inglewood’s public art collection began in the last century as permanent public art and
was incorporated in the construction of City Hall and the Public Library. Concurrent with
those monumental works, a Portable Art Collection of editioned prints on paper by
significant artists were purchased in 1975. Displayed inside City Hall, they are framed
prints by leading artists of the day including Judy Chicago, Gene Davis, Ron Davis and
Leroy Neiman.

The Inglewood Senior Center’s Portable Public Art Collection is largely comprised of
paintings purchased from local artists participating in Inglewood Open Studios 2017.
These works are displayed at the Senior Center in hallways on both floors.

DISCUSSION
IGAP 2020: Inglewood Love will result in a second collection of portable art works on
paper by Inglewood’s leading artists. The project will expeditiously use public art dollars
to purchase existing artworks directly from artists. Direct purchases, unlike commission
projects, will provide income to these artists and do not require contracting or proof of
insurance.

PROCESS
Nominated Inglewood artists will be asked to provide images of up to three works on
paper they would be willing to sell to the City’s Portable Public Art Collection for a set
price not to exceed $1,500. The works will be purchased unframed, to be framed and
 installed in a separate contract. An artist may not propose to create new work for the City;
that would constitute a creative service and require a contract.

To fund the purchase of seven (7) to ten (10) permanent works on paper, 24 x 24” or
smaller, each work’s purchase price shall not exceed $1,500 (minimum $1,000), with local
sales tax included in each purchase. Size limits keep framing affordable.

IGAP 2020: Love Inglewood will result in a collection of unframed works on paper
nominated by and directly purchased from Inglewood artists and may be displayed on the
first floor of Inglewood City Hall.

Professional Inglewood artists will be nominated by Inglewood artists in the public art
collection, former Inglewood Arts Commissioners with arts and design expertise, and
staff. Artists currently in the Inglewood Public Art collection may be reviewed at
https://inglewoodpublicart.org/city-public-art/.

Nominated artists will be invited to submit images of up to three works available for
purchase and made with permanent materials. This would include drawing, water media,
traditional prints and designs, and photographs and digital prints printed on permanent
professional grade paper.

An unpaid panel, comprised of representatives of the departments housed in the civic
facilities where the artworks will be displayed and local contemporary art experts, will
review and select the artwork to be added to the City’s public art collection.

FINANCIAL/FUNDING ISSUES AND SOURCES: This project is funded through the Public
Art Fund - account code 055-070-7010-4870 (Public Art Fund, Contract Services).

DESCRIPTION OF ATTACHMENTS: None

PRESENTER:
Sabrina Barnes, Parks, Recreation & Community Services Director
Helen Lessick, Public Art Consultant

INGLEWOOD  CALIFORNIA

  ARTS COMMISSION

The Arts Commission meeting was held on Wednesday, July 22, 2020 via Zoom. Commissioner Metcalf called the
meeting to order at 6:30 p.m. followed by the flag salute.

Roll Call

  Present
  Commissioner Jacques Lesure, Commissioner at Large
  Commissioner Aletha Metcalf, District 1
  Commissioner Phyllis Battle, District 3
  Commissioner Vicki Banks, District 4
  Sabrina Barnes, Director, Parks, Recreation and Community Services Department
  Helen Lessick, Public Art Consultant
  Stephanie Maldonado, Senior Management Assistant
  Daniel Medina, Senior Recreation Leader
  Absent
  Commissioner Onna Ehrlich-Bell, District 2

Public Comments

  None

Approval of the Minutes

  Commissioner Lesure made a motion to approve the minutes from February 19, 2020. Commissioner Battle
seconded and the minutes were approved as follows:

  Ayes: Commissioners Lessure, Battle, Banks and Metcalf
  Nays: None

Staff Report

  Stephanie Maldonado introduced a staff report recommending the Arts Commission recommend the
Planning Commission and City Council approve the Public Art Plan for the Fairview Heights mixed-use development
at 923 E. Redondo Boulevard. Public Art Consultants: NOW Art LA. Helen Lessick presented a PowerPoint
presentation with an overview and recap of the Public Art Project entitled Rise Above. Commissioners were asked to
consider the following: the art narrative, art design, art site, artist’s qualifications and the budget. Joining in the
discussion was Carmen Zella, Principal of NOW Art who spoke about the art pieces and the community engagement
involvement piece of the project. Commissioner Metcalf asked if National CORE is the Congress of Racial Equality.
Ms. Lessick stated no, it is a nonprofit organization that builds low income and affordable housing. Commissioner
Lessure asked for more detail regarding the community involvement. Ms. Zella explained she and her team gathered
individuals from a list of community partners from Linc Housing which included long term residents and others from
youth organizations. She provided them with a series of ten (10) questions and held a presentation via Zoom where
they discussed the project and went over their thoughts and suggestions. Commissioner Lessure asked if the
  1
   INGLEWOOD  CALIFORNIA

  ARTS COMMISSION

windows where the art will be displayed are residential windows. Ms. Zella stated yes, we are working with a lighting
consultant who will be selecting power lighting for that area and the windows will be tinted. Commissioner Battle
asked if any of the Arts Commissioners were included in the meeting with the community. Ms. Lessick stated no
because it would not have been appropriate for that portion of the process. Ms. Zella stated if possible, she would
love for the Commission to be a part of the narrative and audio portion of the project. Ms. Zella went on to introduce
her team: Shalawn Garcia, Nina Dooley and Denise Petrulis from LINC Housing, and artists Eric Skotnes and Ryan
Sarfati. Sabrina Barnes acknowledged and thanked team for an amazing job at returning a product that we will all be
proud of. Commissioner Battle asked who is responsible for the maintenance of the mural. Ms. Lessick stated the
private developer has their own maintenance plan. Commissioner Lessure asked if the augmented reality (AR)
feature of the project will be (inaudible), stagnant or reflect what is going on in the city at the time. Ms. Barnes stated
the AR is site specific and will speak to the project and nature of the complex.

  Commissioner Battle made a motion to approve the staff report. Commissioner Metcalf seconded and the
staff report was approved as follows:

  Ayes: Commissioners Lessure, Metcalf, Battle and Banks
  Nays: None

  Helen Lessick thanked the Commissioners and the NOW Art team, artists and Linc Housing for such a
fantastic project. Commissioner Battle thinks the mural is beautiful, innovative, and likes the multiple dimensions and
how inviting the space is. She also loves the monthly inspection proposal and the fact that 50 units of the complex will
be set aside for the homeless population. Commissioner Metcalf echoed Commissioner Battle’s sentiments. Sabrina
Barnes informed Ms. Zella of the item moving forward to the Planning Commission tentatively scheduled for August
5th.

  Stephanie Maldonado introduced a staff report recommending the Arts Commission support the
allocation of $12,000 for the Inglewood Growing Artists Projects (IGAP) 2020 program to provide for purchases of
original artworks on a 24 x 24” paper by Inglewood artists as the Inglewood Love collection, to be framed and
displayed in public areas in city facilities. Ms. Lessick stated the IGAP 2020 will establish the City’s 3rd portable Public
Arts Collection through direct purchases of works on paper from nominated Inglewood Artist. The $12,000 will be
used to purchase unframed work for $1,000 to $1,500 each (price to included sales tax). Work will separately be
professionally framed and installed under a separate contract. The City currently has two (2) portable artwork
collections - one located in City Hall and the other is located at the Senior Center. Professional Inglewood artists
will be nominated by Inglewood artists in the public art collection, former Inglewood Arts Commissioners with arts and
design expertise, and staff. Nominated artists will be invited to submit images of up to three works available for
purchase and made with permanent materials. This would include drawing, water media, traditional prints and
designs, and photographs and digital prints printed on permanent professional grade paper. An unpaid panel,
comprised of representatives of the departments housed in the civic facilities where the artworks will be displayed
and local contemporary art experts, will review and select the artwork to be added to the City’s public art collection.

  2
   INGLEWOOD  CALIFORNIA

  ARTS COMMISSION

  Commissioner Lesure made a motion to approve the staff report. Commissioner Battle seconded and the
staff report was approved as follows:

  Ayes: Commissioners Lessure, Metcalf, Battle and Banks
  Nays: None

Verbal Reports Regarding the following Public Art Related Projects

  None

Public Comments

  None

Commissioners’ Comments/Initiatives/Art Calendar

  Commissioner Battle asked for the status on the IGAP music project. Sabrina Barnes stated the artist who
was chosen decided not to sign the City’s contract due insurance requirements. We will revisit the project and rebid
casting a broader net of reach in hopes of capturing a wider number of contenders. Commissioner Lessure asked if
the second runner up was offered the opportunity. Ms. Barnes stated no.

  Commissioner Lessure stated he would like to discuss the music in Inglewood specifically in regards to the
new Disney Center and the Miracle Theater happenings and how the Commission can be a part of it all. He will put it
in writing and request for it to be put on the agenda for a future meeting.

  Commissioner Banks is looking forward to working with everyone on the new and exciting upcoming projects.

  Commissioner Battle is happy to see everyone in good health.

With no further business, the meeting was adjourned at 7:24 p.m.
